newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) has appeared to be heading for a serious split when nearly 40 CDA provincial representatives noisily protested against the academic-led vetting committee's decision to rule out direct elections for senators. The provincial representatives also set up two committees to shadow the vetting committee, which is chaired by former prime minister Anand Panyarachun. (THE NATION)

- Police General Salang Bunnag is resisting moves by the attorney-general to gather further details of his role in the extrajudicial killings of six men in Suphan Buri province last November. The deputy police chief has challenged the authority of Kanit na Nakhon to order police to collect more information on 12 or 13 aspects of the November 27 operation in which the suspected amphetamine dealers died. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government has bowed to fierce industry lobbying and abolishes the recently imposed 10 percent excise tax on marble and granite. The backdown was announced yesterday even as Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan expressed concerns that it could damage the government's credibility as well as the confidence of foreign investors. (BUSINESS DAY) (BANGKOK POST)

- Labour academics are predicting that finance companies will lay off or reduce the salaries of 1,400 middle-level managers this year in an effort to survive. A preliminary survey shows that people employed in the financial sector will be among the hardest hit by the economic slump. (THE NATION)
